facts.text: In 2025/26, 126 workers were killed in Great Britain across industries; the figures are not specific to mines, quarries or construction earthmovers.
facts.quote: In 2025/26, 126 workers were killed in Great Britain

facts.text: In Great Britain's cross-industry 2025/26 worker fatality statistics, struck by moving vehicle was the second most common fatal accident category, with 24 deaths, behind falls from height with 31 deaths.
facts.quote: "struck by moving vehicle" was the second most common kind of fatal accident with 24 deaths, after falls from height (31)

facts.text: Great Britain's cross-industry 2025/26 worker fatality statistics recorded 21 deaths from being struck by moving objects, 18 from being trapped by something collapsing or overturning, and 10 from contact with moving machinery, all below the 24 deaths from moving vehicles.
facts.quote: ahead of struck by moving object (21), trapped by something collapsing or overturning (18) and contact with moving machinery (10)

facts.text: In HSE's 2024/25 release, being struck by a moving vehicle accounted for about 16% of cross-industry fatal injuries in Great Britain.
facts.quote: In the 2024/25 release HSE put being struck by a moving vehicle at about 16% of fatal injuries

facts.text: HSE's 2024/25 release reported an average of around 21 deaths a year from being struck by moving vehicles over the preceding five years, across industries in Great Britain.
facts.quote: averaging around 21 deaths a year over the preceding five years [55]

facts.text: In Great Britain's cross-industry 2023/24 worker fatality figures, being struck by a moving vehicle accounted for 25 of 138 deaths.
A vendor summary of HSE data reported that being struck by a moving vehicle accounted for 14 of 124 worker deaths in Great Britain in 2024/25; these are cross-industry figures.
facts.quote: 14 of 124 (2024/25), the latter figure taken from a vendor summary of HSE data [56, 57]

facts.text: HSE's cross-industry workplace transport guidance states that nearly a quarter of all deaths involving workplace transport occur during reversing; this figure is not specific to mines, quarries or construction earthmovers.
facts.quote: nearly a quarter of all deaths involving Workplace transport occur during reversing

facts.text: HSE's workplace transport guidance states that many reversing accidents cause no injury but cause costly damage to vehicles, equipment and premises; the guidance is cross-industry rather than specific to mines, quarries or construction earthmovers.
facts.quote: many other reversing accidents do not result in injury but cause costly damage to vehicles, equipment and premises

facts.text: HSE's undated quarry guidance Hard Target states that transport accounts for 40% of all accidents in quarries.
facts.quote: transport accounts for 40% of all accidents in quarries and 60% of all deaths

facts.text: HSE's undated quarry guidance Hard Target states that transport accounts for 60% of all deaths in quarries.
facts.quote: transport accounts for 40% of all accidents in quarries and 60% of all deaths

facts.text: HSE's undated quarry guidance Hard Target states that seat belts would prevent 25% of all fatal accidents at quarries.
facts.quote: seat belts "would save 25% of all fatal accidents at quarries"
